NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026
BLUE FLAME
NASA microgravity combustion data turned into clear answers for fire safety in space.
Challenge
Flame in Free Fall: AI-powered fire safety insights from microgravity combustion data
Team SUMO · Carlos Yesid López · Marcela Areiza
The problem
A fire in space has no emergency exit
≈15%
Burns with less oxygen
On the space station, about 15% oxygen is enough for some materials to burn; on Earth it takes about 18%.
30%+
The Moon will be more flammable
Lunar bases and rovers will use 30% oxygen or more at 10.2 psi or less: over 40% above Earth’s air.
24
Data no one compares
NASA PSI’s combustion investigations exist, but they are hard to find, compare and interpret.
Sources: NASA Space Apps 2026 challenge statement · SoFIE-MIST results (UC Berkeley, 2024) · NASA Physical Sciences Informatics
The solution
BLUE FLAME turns 24 investigations into an answer for your scenario
Compares experiments using the same fields and units.
Connects each experiment to spacecraft, the ISS, lunar bases and rovers.
Shows what’s missing: conditions no one has studied.
Is explainable: rules with cited sources, no real-time AI.
User experience
The journey: from question to answer in four steps
1
Experiment
Define your scenario
Choose an environment and set oxygen, pressure, material, gravity and airflow. The flame changes live.
2
Coverage
Measure the risk
Thermometer against the ISS, five factors and a ranking of investigations.
3
Scope
Find the gaps
Combinations and conditions no experiment has studied.
4
Map
Locate your scenario
Oxygen versus pressure against everything studied.
NASA data and technology
From NASA’s archive to a working prototype
01 · Data
NASA PSI
24 combustion investigations: 19 flight experiments (ISS and Cygnus spacecraft) and 5 ground studies.
02 · Extraction
Comparable records
Python and Docker read the public metadata and extract fuel, O₂, pressure and airflow with traceability.
03 · Rules
Cited science
Relevance, gaps and fire favorability based on BASS, SAFFIRE, SoFIE-MIST and FM2.
04 · Prototype
Web dashboard
Four tabs, four languages, works offline and over 50 automated tests.

What the prototype reveals
The dashboard shows the risk and also what we don’t know
+4.5
Far higher than the ISS
Plastic at 41% O₂ and 4.3 psi. Lowering oxygen to 21% brings it below the ISS.
2 of 24
Records with oxygen data
In PSI’s public texts, only 2 investigations report oxygen and 4 report pressure.
0
Partial-gravity data
PSI has no combustion data in lunar or Martian gravity. FM2 and LUCI will fill that gap.
Prototype results using the records extracted from PSI. Fire favorability is indicative and does not replace NASA flammability testing.
Impact and next steps
Safer habitats, from the design stage
Who it’s for
Engineers and designers assess lunar cabins and rovers before building them.
Researchers prioritize the experiments still missing.
Teachers and students see how fire changes in space.
Fire safety on Earth: what we learn improves extinguishers and smoke detection.
Next steps
Verify all 24 records as a team.
Integrate the data from each individual PSI test.
Add lunar-gravity results from FM2 and LUCI.
Expand the analysis to more cabin materials.
